lesson_title: When a Business Becomes a Person
hook_text: Register your business as a company and something strange happens: it becomes a person who can owe money instead of you.
clip_script: Two bakers want three more shops. As partners, every debt could cost them their homes. So they register a company with CIPC, and the business becomes its own legal person: Soweto Bakes Proprietary Limited. Now the company owns the ovens and owes the debts. The most the owners can lose is what they put in. That is limited liability. And if one of them retires, the company carries on. A private company cannot sell shares to the public. A public company can, often on the JSE, but it must open its books to everyone. Buy one hundred shares at fifty rand, and the most you can ever lose is five thousand rand.
visual_style: A whiteboard bakery that stands up with its own name tag, a cake sliced into shares, a shield over two houses, and a stock exchange board ticking up.
mood: Curious and confident, a big idea made simple.
pacing: Strange hook, a steady build through the company's new powers, a crisp private-versus-public contrast, and a number to finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and meet the business that became a person.
